articles.headline: UConn's Dan Hurley overheats in quarter-zip jacket at halftime interview during Syracuse exhibition
keyFacts: UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley complained about his uncomfortable, overheating quarter-zip jacket during a halftime interview in an exhibition game against Syracuse.
Athletic director David Benedict stated on social media that coaches' apparel choices are outside his administrative domain.
UConn improved in the second half, securing a 72-52 win over Syracuse led by Na'jai Hines.
body: UNCASVILLE, CONNECTICUT - OCTOBER 13: Silas Demary Jr. #5 of the Connecticut Huskies reacts after forcing the turnover against Gavin Doty #4 of the Syracuse Orange during the first half of the NCAA men's exhibition basketball game at Mohegan Sun Arena. (Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images)

The frustrations of UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley surprisingly weren't directed toward his new-look squad after an uneven first-half display against Syracuse in Tuesday's exhibition matchup .

Hurley spoke with NBC Sports Boston sideline reporter Kayla Burton for a halftime interview before entering the annals of Mohegan Sun Arena, but an uncomfortable quarter-zip jacket derailed his attempt to offer insight into UConn's first 20 minutes of the season.
"Whatever this is, it feels like a wool," Hurley said about his jacket. "It feels like a straitjacket that they put me in. I can't believe that this is the best that we've got to wear tonight."
Note to self: More breathable material for Dan Hurley https://t.co/cbQ59NRhKH

- Alec Crouthamel (@AlecCr12) October 13, 2026 Hurley's uncomfortable interview drew attention within the UConn community, prompting a few messages to athletic director David Benedict requesting better sideline wear for the eighth-year Huskies head coach. Benedict posted on X Tuesday evening to distance his administration from Hurley's uncomfortable jacket, claiming that the attire of UConn coaches is outside his domain.
"Seriously? I'm responsible for a lot of things but not what our coaches wear, basketball or otherwise," Benedict wrote on X.

With a healthy crowd and marquee opponent at Mohegan Sun Arena, Hurley's casual attire was one of the few indicators that Tuesday's game didn't count in the record books. According to Mid Major Madness, Hurley is one of just 73 college basketball coaches to wear at least a partial suit on game days, making his quarter-zip airflow struggles against the Orange Tuesday doubly surprising.

Hurley and his Huskies looked more comfortable coming out of the locker room, as UConn's 18-5 run midway through the second half put the exhibition out of reach down the stretch. Na'jai Hines led the Huskies with 17 points and eight rebounds as UConn secured a 72-52 win.

articles.headline: Judge extends White House access to banned media outlets CNN, MS Now and Politico
keyFacts: A federal judge ordered the White House on Tuesday to continue allowing journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to access the building as the media coalition’s lawsuit against the Trump administration plays out.

Timothy Kelly, a district court judge, had on 24 September granted a 14-day reprieve for the news organizations, which six days earlier had been banned by the president in an extraordinary move from entering the White House grounds “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS”.
The organizations filed a lawsuit on 21 September seeking to overturn the ban as a violation of their rights under the US constitution.
body: A federal judge ordered the White House on Tuesday to continue allowing journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico to access the building as the media coalition’s lawsuit against the Trump administration plays out.

Timothy Kelly, a district court judge, had on 24 September granted a 14-day reprieve for the news organizations, which six days earlier had been banned by the president in an extraordinary move from entering the White House grounds “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS”.

“Defendants (except for President Trump) and their agents, representatives, and all persons or entities acting in concert with them, shall not execute, implement, or enforce the September 18, 2026, decision to revoke the White House ‘hard pass’ press credentials held by employees of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO, thereby maintaining the status quo since the Court’s entry of a temporary restraining order on September 24, 2026,” the judge wrote in granting a preliminary injunction requested by the plaintiffs.

The organizations filed a lawsuit on 21 September seeking to overturn the ban as a violation of their rights under the US constitution. But that temporary restraining order expired on Tuesday, bringing the media companies into court late last week to ask for a preliminary injunction that would lift the ban during the duration of the lawsuit, which could take months.

During arguments at the E Barrett Prettyman Federal Courthouse in Washington, Kelly seemed inclined to lift the ban indefinitely, telling a lawyer for the federal government that his side had “a notice problem” that was “probably the biggest hurdle” they had to overcome.

The Trump White House gave no advance notice to the media companies affected to say that they were at risk of losing their press badges, which the news organizations have said are essential to their ability to cover the administration. While the White House sent letters to the media companies informing them of the ban, they did so post-hoc, after building access had already been cut off, in violation of binding court precedent.

In his ruling on Tuesday, Judge Kelly wrote that the plaintiffs “are likely to succeed not only on their due process claim, but also on their two First Amendment claims”. While access to the White House is not guaranteed, court precedent dictates that once it is provided to journalists, it cannot be taken away for editorial or viewpoint-based reasons.

During arguments for a preliminary injunction on 8 October, media lawyer Theodore J Boutrous told the judge that Trump had offered a “confession” – in a Time magazine interview last week – that he was banning the media companies explicitly because of the content of their reporting, not because of any other considerations, such as national security.
“The case has gotten stronger for the plaintiffs thanks to President Trump,” Boutrous told the judge.

The judge seemed to agree. “President Trump’s own comments suggest that he intended the revocation of Plaintiffs’ hard passes to alter their reporting on him, bolstering the case that his action here is sufficient to deter a reporter of ordinary firmness from reporting in the same way she had before,” he wrote.

Although the White House has largely adhered to the judge’s prior ruling restoring access on a temporary basis, journalists for CNN and Politico have on occasion been prevented from performing “pool duty” – covering the daily activities of the president – because the administration has interpreted the judge’s temporary restraining order to solely require access to the White House complex, not smaller spaces like Air Force One or the Oval Office.
The judge required the media plaintiffs to post a bond of $1.

In a statement, Boutrous said of the judge’s ruling: “When the President issued his ‘ban on the free press,’ he blatantly and explicitly violated due process and the First Amendment. Since then, the President has repeatedly, candidly, and consistently admitted in public that he banned our clients from the White House to punish reporting he doesn’t like and to try to force journalists to cover him in ways he prefers.”
The court, he added, “was right to enjoin the White House from enforcing this ‘unconstitutional ban on the free press’ for the foreseeable future”.

articles.headline: Tracy McGrady gets honest about how the Timberwolves can be the dark horse in the West
keyFacts: NBA legend Tracy McGrady stated that the Minnesota Timberwolves could disrupt the Western Conference favorites in the 2026-27 season.
The Timberwolves added guard LaMelo Ball in the offseason to join Anthony Edwards in the backcourt, according to the article.
McGrady said Ball will improve the team's offense, reduce scoring pressure on Edwards late in games, and create scoring opportunities for Rudy Gobert.
body: Ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season, two teams stand out in the Western Conference. Those are the two Western Conference Finals teams: the Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs. That feels unanimous to a lot of people, but other teams seem to be looking to pull off surprises.

Multiple teams made some big changes in the offseason, including the Minnesota Timberwolves. With the addition of LaMelo Ball in the backcourt, they could be one of the most dangerous teams in the league, as that offensive boost is a big deal.
Tracy McGrady lauds the Timberwolves' potential to upset the West favorites

Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch has plenty of weapons in his arsenal now. In the past, he had to work with a limited backcourt that was spearheaded by Anthony Edwards. Mike Conley was a tremendous player, but he was struggling to keep up with his younger counterpart.

Now, Edwards has a more dynamic partner in LaMelo Ball. Not only are they the top players from the 2020 Draft, but they also have a similar attitude about them that makes them such a fun fit alongside each other. While it is a fun duo, the jury is still out on whether it can work out in the long term.

If someone asks NBA legend Tracy McGrady about this team, he will say that he is extremely high on them. In fact, he has picked them as the team that could disrupt that Thunder and Spurs duo at the top of the Western Conference in the 2026-27 season.

"I'm putting some stock in that right there. Reason being, I think this is the first time LaMelo has played in meaningful games. He's playing with a team that has been to the Western Conference Finals, guys that are serious about winning ball games," McGrady said on NBA on NBC about the Western Conference's dark horse.

"What he's going to unlock for that team offensively is not having that pressure on Ant Man to score when it's late in the games. The pace is going to be up and down. I think he's going to unlock Rudy Gobert with some lob threats."

McGrady is bringing up some valid points that make the Timberwolves such a dangerous team. Ball is such a dynamic addition that the rest of the NBA has to be wary because they are ready to make some noise and disrupt what people have projected.

articles.headline: China and North Korea to open New Yalu River Bridge, state media reports
keyFacts: China and North Korea will officially open the New Yalu River Bridge to traffic on Thursday, China’s state-run Xinhua news agency reported.
China completed its side of the bridge in 2014 to boost trade, but North Korea delayed finishing its side after relations strained over nuclear sanctions.
China remains North Korea's key economic partner, while North Korea has recently expanded military ties with Russia.
body: China and North Korea will officially open the New Yalu River Bridge to traffic on Thursday, China’s state-run Xinhua news agency reports.

China completed its side of the bridge in 2014, hoping to boost trade ties. However, North Korea left its side unfinished for years as relations soured after Beijing supported United Nations sanctions over Pyongyang’s nuclear tests.
The first bridge connecting Russia and North Korea also opened earlier this month.
China-North Korea Relations

China’s exports to North Korea rose to a six-year high of $2.3bn last year, a 25 percent increase from the previous year. Chinese President Xi Jinping was welcomed in Pyongyang in June for the first time since 2019.
Since 2018, Beijing has tried to repair ties with Pyongyang, which also briefly began improving relations with Washington around the same time.

The China-North Korea relationship was forged during the Korean War. In 1961, the two countries signed the Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance, which remains China’s only formal military alliance.
The treaty contains a mutual defence clause committing either side to assist the other if one comes under armed attack.

Although China was North Korea’s main diplomatic partner and protector for decades, relations strained after Beijing in 2017 supported tightening sanctions on Pyongyang for its nuclear weapons programme.
Analysts say North Korea’s recent growing relationship with Russia may have changed the balance of Pyongyang’s diplomatic dependence, reducing its reliance on Beijing.

North Korea and Russia signed a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty in 2024, including a mutual defence provision. Military and political ties between the two countries have grown considerably stronger, with North Korea deploying thousands of troops to fight in Russia’s war on Ukraine.

United States President Donald Trump also signalled an interest in repairing relations with Pyongyang last month, after his talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un abruptly ended in 2019. In his second term, Trump has floated meeting Kim again, though no official meeting has been set.
North Korea has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.
While North Korea’s trade with Russia largely involves military supplies, exchanges with China could arguably involve goods North Korea needs to develop its civilian economy, analysts have said.

articles.headline: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
keyFacts: Missiles and drones were intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition struck a fuel depot near Sanaa, coalition officials said.
The Houthis warned they would target Saudi infrastructure in retaliation for coalition airstrikes on territory they control in Yemen.
The ongoing civil war and escalating attacks have caused civilian casualties, displacement, and concerns over fuel supplies and oil prices.
body: - Published
Missiles and drones have been intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says.

Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said projectiles targeting the Saudi capital and other cities were intercepted. No casualties have been reported however fires broke out at Saudi oil company Aramco's building in Dhahran after the strike, officials said.
It comes after the coalition struck the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility on Tuesday night.
The latest tit-for-tat attacks in the conflict "have potentially negative spillovers for everybody, everywhere", the chief of the the International Monetary Fund said.
The Houthis warned they would target the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam.
It came as the Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the Iran-backed group would "bear the consequences" of its recent deadly attacks on the kingdom.
Thirteen people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, while another person was killed in a similar attack there the following day.
On Tuesday, the coalition said its forces had destroyed three drones north of Riyadh.

The Houthis have said they are targeting airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones in response to deadly Saudi strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including Sanaa.
The Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces mounting an offensive on Yemen's Red Sea coast and several other front lines.

A correspondent for AFP news agency reported that queues formed at petrol stations in Sanaa on Tuesday afternoon following the coalition's warning of an impending operation against the al-Sabaha oil facility, with many residents worried about shortages.
The Yemen Petroleum Company, which is run by the Houthis, issued a statement that sought to reassure them, saying the facility "does not contain any stock of petroleum products".

The company also said it had "taken all necessary precautionary measures to address any emergency, ensuring the stability of the supply situation and the continued meeting of citizens' needs in a normal manner".

After al-Maliki confirmed the strike, first reported by Houthi media, explosions were heard over Riyadh and other Saudi cities, with al-Maliki reporting four missiles and two drones had been intercepted near the capital.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.
US President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on Tuesday the Houthis were "behaving very badly... and purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices".
Speaking to reporters, he did not answer a question on whether he'd made a decision to help the Saudis retaliate against them, but said he "might" ask Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan to intervene.
Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes.
Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed in Yemen since August. The UN's human rights office says they include at least 54 civilians, half of them children.
More than 216,000 people have also been displaced across the country, and suspected cholera cases have tripled in three weeks, rising from 217 to 647, according to the UN.

articles.headline: 10 Sci-Fi Books You Need to Read Before You Die
keyFacts: Polygon published a reading list highlighting ten essential science fiction books that push the boundaries of storytelling and reality.
The curated list features a diverse mix of works ranging from early dystopian classics like Yevgeny Zamyatin's We to modern hard sci-fi like Liu Cixin's The Three-Body Problem.
The selection includes influential novels and short story collections that explore complex themes such as human identity, political dissent, and virtual reality.
body: Sci-fi remains one of the most expansive playgrounds for storytelling, capable of charting distant galaxies and alien frontiers just as easily as it exposes the immediate horrors of modern-day technology. At its peak, speculative fiction uses its invented worlds and distant planets to interrogate what it means to be human, cracking open philosophical questions that grounded genres simply can’t reach.

Distilling the essential sci-fi canon into a single reading list is a formidable task. Pillars like Dune and 1984 built the genre's bedrock, but some of speculative fiction's most brilliant feats lie along far stranger, less-traveled paths. Short story collections, hallucinatory mind-benders, and sociopolitical thought experiments have constantly redrawn the boundary lines of what a sci-fi narrative can achieve. Some of these still prove the most essential reading to this day.
Whether you’re seeking a genre-defining landmark or a cult masterpiece, these essential sci-fi novels demonstrate just how far this kind of fiction can push the boundaries of reality.
10 Beyond the Curve (1991) by Kōbō Abe

Kōbō Abe's Beyond the Curve is vital for the intrepid sci-fi reader. This collection of 12 short stories span Abe’s 17-year career, from 1949 to 1966. Beyond the Curve is a compendium of strange tales that operate more like fever dreams than narratives. In “Dendrocacalia,” a bewildered man begins to transform into a plant, while “The Crime of S. Karma” follows a person who discovers his name has abandoned him.

Abe approaches these increasingly surreal scenarios with a matter-of-factness that makes them all the more unsettling, blending science fiction, dark comedy, and existential horror to explore the fragility of identity and the absurdity of modern life. The author may well be more celebrated for The Woman in the Dunes and other fantastic novels, but his shorter work commands equal reverence from readers seeking the genre’s eerie fringes.
9 The Invention of Morel (1940) by Adolfo Bioy Casares

What if the people standing beside you were mere ghosts of light? That haunting premise drives Adolfo Bioy Casares’ The Invention of Morel, a novella following a desperate fugitive who stumbles onto an island thought abandoned, only to find a mysterious enclave of tourists trapped in loops like the Hosts of Westworld. Their baffling behavior pulls him toward a terrifying technological breakthrough with profound implications for human memory and mortality.

Published in 1940, Casares' masterwork predates modern virtual reality and simulation theory, yet uncannily predicts our obsession with preserving experience and lost affection. It’s a stark reminder that a speculative masterpiece doesn't need a sweeping cosmic canvas to leave a permanent emotional scar.
8 Snow Crash (1992) by Neal Stephenson

Much like Adolfo Bioy Casares, Neal Stephenson imagined a world where people escaped their reality into a virtual environment, but things get far more action-packed in this cyberpunk thrill ride. The story of Snow Crash follows Hiro Protagonist, a hacker and pizza-delivery driver who becomes embroiled in a conspiracy involving a mysterious digital drug, ancient Sumerian mythology, and the relationship between language and the human brain.

Stephenson's novel helped popularize the term "metaverse" and remains a foundational cyberpunk text, even as some of its predictions have aged in unexpected ways. Its corporate-run enclaves, privatized infrastructure, and fragmented society feel particularly recognizable today, especially for fans of Cyberpunk 2077 and Blade Runner.
7 We (1921) by Yevgeny Zamyatin

Published decades before 1984 and Brave New World, Yevgeny Zamyatin's We helped establish the blueprint for the modern dystopian novel. Its protagonist, D-503, lives in a society governed by mathematical precision, where citizens surrender their individuality to the authority of a government known as the One State. Even their daily routines are regulated, and the glass walls of their homes leave little room for privacy, something eerily reminiscent of the prevalence of digital surveillance today.

Zamyatin's greatest trick with We is making this world feel both absurd and frighteningly logical. Written in 1921, amid the ideological aftermath of the Russian Revolution, We was deemed an existential threat by early Soviet censors and promptly banned. It spent decades surviving in secret printings before being published abroad, casting an inescapable shadow over the entire genre. We remains a vital masterpiece that, almost a century later, still proves sci-fi is often at its most potent when turned into a weapon of political dissent.
6 Ubik (1969) by Philip K. Dick

Trying to explain the plot of Ubik without spoiling its sci-fi pleasures is nearly impossible, but that’s the beauty in Philip K. Dick. The novel opens in a hyper-capitalist 1992, when corporate espionage is fought between spy agencies and "inertials," anti-psychics hired to block telepathic industrial theft. When field technician Joe Chip and his employer, Glen Runciter, take a team of inertials to the Moon to secure a client's facility, an explosive ambush throws the mission into chaos.

Dick turned the camera inward at a time when most hard sci-fi relied on grand space adventures and time travel, pioneering a psychological framework that redefined the genre. Ubik is the crucial bridge connecting mid-century speculative fiction to the cyberpunk and simulation-theory classics that followed, laying the conceptual groundwork for everything from The Matrix and Dark City to Satoshi Kon’s Paprika. Dick delivered a masterclass in philosophical sci-fi simply by transforming mundane commercialism into a divine force. More than five decades later, it still proves that the most terrifying frontier in speculative fiction isn't deep space, but the human mind.
5 The Three-Body Problem (2008) by Liu Cixin

First contact is usually treated as an opportunity for terror, popularized best in H. G. Wells’ War of the Worlds. Other times, it can be represented as wonder, like Carl Sagan’s Contact, or even a combination of the two. Liu Cixin's The Three-Body Problem takes a colder approach, asking instead what humanity's place in the universe might look like if the civilizations beyond Earth operate according to rules we barely understand. Beginning amid the upheaval of China's Cultural Revolution, the novel moves into a scientific mystery involving an alien civilization struggling to survive in an unpredictable planetary system.

Liu combines theoretical questions with a gripping mystery, gradually expanding the scale of the narrative until humanity itself becomes only a small piece of a much grander puzzle. The novel helped bring Chinese science fiction to an international audience, and its uncompromising cosmic perspective, now poart of a trilogy, makes it one of the defining works of modern hard sci-fi.
4 A Canticle for Leibowitz (1959) by Walter M. Miller Jr.

A Canticle for Leibowitz tracks the monks of the Albertian Order of Leibowitz in the deserts of the American Southwest as they painstakingly preserve the "Memorabilia,” a scattered collection of blueprint fragments, shopping lists, and technical manuals saved from an anti-intellectual backlash. Divided into three distinct eras separated by centuries, the narrative watches humanity claw its way out of a dark age of illiteracy, rediscover electrical power and nuclear technology, and inevitably build toward the same catastrophic precipice once again.

Walter M. Miller Jr. constructs a dark and ironic historical cycle where the very church keeping the light of human knowledge alive must watch in horror as civilization uses that salvaged intelligence to engineer its own destruction. Miller, a former WWII bomber radioman haunted by the destruction of the Monte Cassino monastery, fused humor and speculative history into a warning against forgetting our dark past.
3 Foundation (1951) by Isaac Asimov

Normally, I’d call out The Gods Themselves, but Isaac Asimov's Foundation feels more essential reading for sci-fi fans. If anything, it’s the quintessential space opera spanning years of fictional history, like J.R.R. Tolkien's The Silmarillion but for sci-fi. The story starts first with Hari Seldon, a mathematician who develops a science called psychohistory. He believes he can shorten the dark age that’s set to come for the Galactic Empire, preserving knowledge and guiding the future through a series of carefully planned crises over the course of centuries.

The resulting story is less concerned with individual heroes than with the rise and fall of civilizations, making politics, economics, and historical forces the real engines of its drama. Asimov's vision helped define the grand scale of modern space opera, influencing generations of writers who wanted to imagine the future in terms of entire societies rather than single adventures. It's hard to overstate the ambition of a series that treats the fate of a galaxy as a problem to be solved, and while it does toss away characters quicker than Game of Thrones at times, the overarching text is gripping to the last word.
2 Hyperion (1989) by Dan Simmons

Dan Simmons takes an unconventional approach to space opera in Hyperion, structuring the novel around a group of seven pilgrims traveling a fatal journey to the mysterious Time Tombs of a dying world. Drawing directly on the framework of The Canterbury Tales, each pilgrim recounts their personal history during the voyage, allowing Simmons to seamlessly shift tones and subgenres across the anthology of their lives.

The result is a book that feels far larger than its central quest. Each narrative reveals another exciting corner of a richly imagined future. Rather than leaning on conventional space battle tropes, Simmons uses his disparate characters — a tormented priest, a battle-hardened soldier, a grieving scholar whose daughter ages backward, a cynical poet, a detective, and a Templar — to interrogate humanity’s gravest fascinations.
1 The Left Hand of Darkness (1969) by Ursula K. Le Guin

Ursula K. Le Guin's The Left Hand of Darkness is one of those rare science fiction novels that can permanently change how you think about the world you inhabit. Set on the perpetually frozen world of Gethen, the novel follows Genly Ai, a lone human envoy sent by an interstellar confederation to invite the planet's nations into a peaceful alliance. His diplomatic mission falters not just against treacherous court intrigue and xenophobic cold wars, but against his own deeply ingrained prejudices. As Genly traverses icy landscapes with the exiled Gethenian statesman Estraven, their grueling trek transforms from a political survival story into a quiet journey of mutual understanding across an immense cultural divide.

Le Guin’s thought experiment dismantled centuries of gender assumptions by asking what a society looks like without rigid gender roles, innate male dominance, or gender-driven warfare. Beyond its pioneering gender critique, the novel also stands as a timeless meditation on patriotism versus nationalism, the warmth of human connection against existential isolation, and the sheer difficulty of loving someone whose worldview radically differs from your own. It remains a masterclass in how speculative fiction can strip away our daily biases to reveal what it truly means to be human.

articles.headline: How to go Trick-or-Treating in Disney Dreamlight Valley
keyFacts: Disney Dreamlight Valley features a new Trick-or-Treat gameplay mechanic during its annual event.
Players can collect candy once per day from six participating villager houses by interacting with lit jack-o-lanterns.
The Trick-or-Treat event runs from October 14 to 31, offering six recipe rewards for completing specific duties.
body: Disney Dreamlight Valley’s annual Trick-or-Treat event is back for another run, but this time around, it’s introducing a new gameplay feature. We can finally actually go Trick-or-Treating around the village in this event.

Since this mechanic wasn’t always part of the event, there’s a decent chance you may be unsure how to use it. You’re not given any guidance for it, so it can be tricky to figure out at first. If you’re having trouble making it happen, here’s how to go Trick-or-Treating in Disney Dreamlight Valley .

How to Trick-or-Treat in Disney Dreamlight Valley

Screenshot by Destructoid To go Trick-or-Treating for the Trick-or-Treat event in DDV , you need to visit the homes of participating characters, interact with the jack-o’-lantern in front of their house, and claim some Candy as a reward. Here’s a full breakdown of how to navigate this process.
Visit the home of a participating villager. Not all characters found around the valley are part of this task, so the first step is finding characters who are participating in the festivities.

Look for and interact with a lit jack-o’-lantern. You can only go Trick-or-Treating at the house if the jack-o’-lantern is lit up. If it is, walk up to it and press the button that appears next to the “Trick or Treat!” message.

Collect your Candy. As soon as you interact with the jack-o’-lantern, the villager who lives inside will pop out to give you some event Candy as a prize. Each time you visit a participating villager’s home, you get five Green Candies, five Red Candies, and five Purple Candies.
You can only visit a villager’s house once per day. After you have collected Candy from them, the jack-o’-lantern light will go out, signifying that they’re done for the day.

articles.headline: Trump pardons diesel mechanics ‘wrongfully charged’ during Biden admin at Alaska rally
keyFacts: President Trump granted unconditional pardons to two diesel truck mechanics, Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming, during a rally in Alaska.
Czubak and Fleming had pleaded guilty in 2022 to conspiracy to violate the Clean Air Act for tampering with vehicle monitoring and pollution equipment.
The Biden Justice Department previously alleged the men removed required air pollution controls on at least 37 vehicles between 2019 and 2020.
body: President Trump pardoned two diesel truck mechanics at an Alaska rally Tuesday night, arguing they were “wrongfully charged” during the Biden administration.

Trump signed the pardons for Zachary Czubak and Patrick Fleming midway through his midterm election rally in Wasilla for Sen. Dan Sullivan and Rep. Nick Begich, the GOP incumbents in their respective Senate and House races.
“They wanted to put them in jail for 10 years because they fixed an engine,” Trump said. “How sick.”
“Well, I heard about it. I read the story about it. Did a little check, and I’m giving each one an unconditional pardon,” he continued.
White House aide Natalie Harp brought the pardons up to the podium for the president to sign.

“I don’t know if you’ve ever heard, when you give somebody a pardon they say that means – and I don’t know how this works and why it’s an expression, but it’s well used – that means you’re as clean as a newborn baby’s ass,” he quipped.
The president invited the two men up on stage to receive the freshly inked pardons and address the crowd.
“This means the world to me. It’s everything,” Fleming said.

“We’re not criminals. We’re not trying to hurt anybody. We want to help Alaskans. We want to help people with diesel trucks, with vehicles, you know, across the world, and President Trump is showing his support in this, and from the bottom of my heart, I can’t thank him enough,” he added.
Fleming and Czubak both pleaded guilty in 2022 to one count of conspiracy to violate the Clean Air Act.

They allegedly tampered with federally mandated monitoring devices on private and commercial diesel vehicles and removed required air pollution control equipment on at least 37 vehicles between July 2019 and September 2020, according to the Biden Justice Department.
Fleming was given a $66,000 fine, while Czubak was sentenced to five years’ probation and also fined $66,000.
“Enjoy your lives, fellas,” Trump remarked as they left the stage, calling the charges against them “crazy.”
The president also warned Alaskans about a “fake Dan Sullivan” that is on the ballot in the state.
Trump charged that the “fake” Sullivan, a retired teacher, was “put up by the Democrats.”

“It’s just cheating. It’s terrible … They found a guy named Dan Sullivan and they put him up to get people a little confused,” he continued, noting that the 2.4% the other Sullivan received in the ranked-choice Senate primary – allowing him to qualify for the general election – “could be the difference” in November.

articles.headline: Apple will give your older Apple TV a new lease on life with Siri AI
keyFacts: Apple confirmed that Siri AI will arrive on older Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd Generation models via a free software update.
The software update will be available as a beta in select countries and territories in English.
TechRadar reported that they will report back once Apple announces an exact release date for the software update.
body: - Siri AI is coming to Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd Gen
- Free software update arriving later this year
- Update will be available in select countries and territories

While much of the attention on the new Apple TV 4K — now in its fourth generation — may focus on the sticker shock of the $299 / £299 / AU$449 price, it also brings some notable features. Siri AI offers a more robust personal assistant experience via the Siri Remote or the box's far-field microphones. It also has a faster processor to speed things up and supports four HomePod 2 or HomePod mini 2 speakers in a surround setup.

But if you were really hoping to use Siri AI on Apple’s streaming box, maybe to pull up recommendations friends might have suggested or to figure out whether a character is based on a real person, and you don’t want to spend the extra cash on an upgrade, I've got good news.

Alongside announcing the Apple TV 4K (4th generation), Apple has confirmed that Siri AI will arrive on older Apple TV models via a forthcoming software update. The release note reads, “Siri AI is available as a beta on Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later), and is available at launch in the U.S., Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and the UK in English.”

That means the AI-powered, more personalized Siri will arrive on the Apple TV 4K 2nd Gen, 3rd Gen, and the new 4th generation, which begins shipping on November 13, 2026. And since the newest model will launch with Siri AI, that might hint at when Apple will roll out the tvOS 27.2 software update to the other two models. As a reminder, the 2nd Gen shipped in 2021, and the 3rd Gen launched in 2022.

That’s excellent news, because the new Siri AI isn’t just better at basic tasks; it also brings broader knowledge and personal context. So whether it’s pulling up an album your best friend recommended weeks ago that you can’t quite remember, or trying to recount a specific episode you and a family member were up to, the assistant can tap into that info to answer the query.

I saw a few demos of that on the new Apple TV 4K, and even though these older models have less power under the hood, Apple hasn’t said that Siri AI’s features will be limited. So while they could be a hair or two slower, it should still be a strong experience.

Further, if nothing else, it’s a free upgrade that gives you another way to interact with Apple TV and find content. Beyond the added personal queries, you can also get richer recommendations and suggestions when you ask Siri for content.

So, with a free, forthcoming update for Apple TV 4K 2nd and 3rd Gen that’ll bring Siri AI to select areas, and the fact that you can get the Siri Remote for a price, these two additions will bring some new features and could very well make the Apple TV 4K feel fresh again.

articles.headline: Peralta shines as Rays seize on Ramírez error to level ALCS against Guardians
keyFacts: The Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 on Tuesday to tie the American League Championship Series at 1-1.
Freddy Peralta pitched six innings and struck out six batters to earn the win for the Rays.
Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is scheduled for Thursday night in Cleveland.
body: Freddy Peralta pitched six innings of four-hit ball, Liam Hicks lined a two-run single after a fielding error by José Ramírez and the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 3-1 on Tuesday night to level the American League Championship Series at 1-1.
Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Thursday night in Cleveland.

Ramírez, whose two-run homer in Game 5 of the AL Division Series against Chicago helped the Guardians become the 11th team to overcome a 2-0 deficit in a best-of-five series, misplayed a grounder in the fourth inning that led to three unearned runs against rookie left-hander Parker Messick.

Junior Caminero walked to start the inning and Victor Mesa Jr grounded into a forceout that was originally ruled a double play. The Rays challenged the calls at both first and second base, and Mesa was ruled safe after a video review overturned first-base umpire Mark Ripperger’s decision.
After Jonny DeLuca struck out, Chandler Simpson beat out a high chopper to shortstop, and Mesa reached third standing up when Ramírez failed to cover the bag.

Ben Williamson followed with a grounder that scooted under Ramírez’s glove and between his legs after the ball hit the edge where the artificial turf met the infield dirt. The third baseman played back rather than charging.
Williamson reached second and Simpson advanced to third. Hicks drove the next pitch to right-center for a 3-0 lead, electrifying the towel-waving, cowbell-ringing crowd of 32,125 at Tropicana Field.
Peralta and three relievers needed no more support.

With fans chanting “Freddy! Freddy! Freddy!”, Peralta struck out six to earn the win. He was fired up as he walked off the mound in the sixth after striking out Petey Halpin swinging on a full-count changeup.
Kevin Kelly recorded two outs in the seventh, retiring Ramírez on a fly ball to center with two runners on.
Left-hander Ian Seymour replaced him, and Chase DeLauter lined an RBI double into the right-field corner.

Seymour struck out Jo Adell swinging on a changeup, stranding runners at second and third. He pitched a perfect eighth before Bryan Baker retired the side in order in the ninth for his fourth postseason save.
Acquired by the Rays from the Mets at the trade deadline, Peralta turned his season around in Tampa Bay, going 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts after posting a 4.99 ERA for New York.
Messick, who grew up attending Rays games at Tropicana Field, took the loss after allowing six hits and three unearned runs in five innings.
Cleveland had won four straight postseason games for the first time since winning their first six playoff games in 2016 on their way to a World Series berth.
The 98-win Rays swept the New York Yankees in the Division Series before losing Monday’s ALCS opener 7-3.

articles.headline: Steam now has a maddening bouncing logo screensaver, and I'm pretty sure it doesn't perfectly hit the corners
keyFacts: Valve released a major Steam client update that brings the previously beta-only Big Picture Mode screensaver feature to the general public.
The update includes a retro-inspired bouncing Steam logo screensaver that changes color when it hits the screen edges, alongside other performance improvements.
Valve also improved startup performance, added an experimental video codec called Pyrowave for Remote Play, and included tweaks for Linux users.
body: The Steam client got a major new update today, with Big Picture Mode receiving the brunt of the attention. Most exciting, I guess, is that the previously beta-only screensaver feature for Big Picture Mode is now live for the general public. In its default mode the screensaver will display art from recently played games, as well as any recent screenshots you've taken. But you can add your own custom screensavers too, which is nice.

Valve also has "a retro inspired bouncing logo screensaver" which you can select in the new dropdown menu found under Settings / Customization. As the name implies, the Steam logo bounces around a black screen, changing color every time it hits an edge. Valve has not made this screensaver the default screensaver, and it's lucky that it didn't: it's a work of diabolical cruelty. It will drive you to despair.

The screensaver references the ye olde screensaver built into DVD players in the late '90s and early '00s. If you're too young to remember it firsthand you've probably heard of it: a DVD Video logo bounces around a black screen, changing color every time it hits an edge. This unassuming but actually-quite-psychologically-damaging display has gone viral several times over the last decade or so, to the extent that, if you Google it, the Google logo will bounce around the search results page. It even has a Wikipedia page.

Why? Everyone subjected to it in the pre-social media era seems to have experienced the same intense desire for that DVD Video logo to perfectly hit the corner of the television's display. And how often does that happen? Extremely rarely.
If you don't know what I'm talking about, it's essential that you watch this ten hour video of the DVD Video screensaver:

People say smartphone screens are ruining our lives, undermining our attention, destroying literacy etcetera, and I mostly agree. But at least they've saved us from the hypnotic tyranny of the goddamned bouncing DVD logo screensaver. Screw that thing.

Anyway, Valve has its own version now, and after watching it—mostly against my will—for about half-an-hour while I ate my lunch, I'm pretty sure this abhorrent thing never pays out with a perfect corner-hitting moment.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
My suggestion? Don't even think about it. Don't even turn it on as a joke. You may never re-emerge.

Back on topic, though, this Steam client update is genuinely huge compared to the norm. Startup performance has been "improved" to some unspecified degree, for example. A new experimental video codec, Pyrowave, has been added to Remote Play which apparently "allows high bandwidth, low latency video streaming". Linux users get a whole bunch of tweaks and fixes too. But the focus is very much on minor improvements to Big Picture Mode, which is good news for Steam Machine and Deck users.
The update notes in their voluminous glory are here. And I repeat: don't go near the bouncing logo screensaver.

Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. articles.headline: Ossoff denies 2028 plans, commits to six-year Senate term if reelected
keyFacts: Sen. Jon Ossoff pledged during a debate to serve a full six-year term if reelected and stated he has zero interest in running for president.
Rep. Mike Collins claimed during the debate that Ossoff is playing the long game and would ultimately seek the White House.
Ossoff reported having $42.5 million in cash on hand for his reelection campaign according to Federal Election Commission filings.
body: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) reaffirmed his commitment to serve out his full Senate term if reelected, once again quashing speculation that he is eyeing a 2028 presidential bid .

Ossoff was pressed on the possibility of running for president during a debate against his Senate opponent, Rep. Mike Collins (R-GA), Tuesday. When asked if he would pledge to serve the full six-year term, Ossoff answered in the affirmative.
“Yes, I will,” Ossoff said. “I have zero interest in running for president. I’m not running for president. I’m running for reelection to the Senate.”

Rumors have begun swirling this year about Ossoff aiming for the Oval Office following his pointed criticism of President Donald Trump . In August, he accused the president of neglecting his duties to build a White House ballroom and travel with aide Natalie Harp, prompting a personal response from Trump and attacks from White House officials.

Additionally, Ossoff has proven to be a giant in the fundraising sphere. According to Federal Election Commission filings, the Democrat had a whopping $42.5 million in cash on hand at the end of June.
Ossoff is the only incumbent Democratic senator in the 2026 elections defending his seat in a state that Trump won in 2024.

Collins followed up Ossoff’s presidential ambition denials on the debate stage by claiming the Democrat is playing the long game and would ultimately seek the White House. Collins also said Ossoff would move further left in 2028.
THE DEMOCRATS WHO COULD RUN FOR PRESIDENT IN 2028
“He is running for president. He’s going to be your DSA candidate,” Collins said, alleging Ossoff would lean into the socialist movement.

The Cook Political Report rates the Georgia Senate race as “likely Democratic.” A RealClearPolitics average of six surveys taken between Sept. 10-23 of Georgia voters showed that Ossoff had a 7.8-percentage-point advantage over Collins, 51% to 43.2%.

articles.headline: Rep. Ilhan Omar’s relatives subpoenaed by feds as DHS investigates lawmaker’s immigration history
keyFacts: Federal investigators issued subpoenas to relatives of Representative Ilhan Omar as part of a criminal fraud investigation into her family immigration history.
The subpoenas followed a Homeland Security Investigations raid on the home shared by Omar and her husband, and a separate financial disclosure inquiry.
Omar denied any wrongdoing and accused officials of weaponizing federal law enforcement to intimidate political enemies, while her office attributed asset increases to an accounting discrepancy.
body: Relatives of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) have reportedly been issued subpoenas as part of the federal probe into the Somalia-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.
The subpoenas went out to Omar’s sister, Sahra Noor, and at least one other member of her family as part of the ongoing criminal fraud investigation, the New York Times reported on Tuesday.

Noor is the author of a recently published memoir about immigrating from Somalia. She also runs a Minneapolis-based consulting firm that touts having secured “more than $20 million in funding for health initiatives and consulted on projects backed by” the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, United States Agency for International Development and other groups.
Noor did not immediately respond to The Post’s request for comment.

Federal investigators have been looking into the immigration history of Omar’s family, including whether the congresswoman’s late father, Nur Omar Mohamed, lied or omitted information on immigration forms before becoming a citizen, the outlet reported.

Omar’s 2022 congressional primary opponent, AJ Kern, obtained documents from a US Citizenship and Immigration Services information officer in 2023 showing “no record” of Nur Omar Mohamed having been naturalized as a US citizen, The Post reported earlier Monday.
The subpoena revelation comes one day after Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) raided the home Omar shares with her husband, Tim Mynett.
Omar has vehemently denied any wrongdoing and has accused the Trump administration of weaponizing federal law enforcement in an effort to intimidate her.

“I’m ok. Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar said in a statement on X. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”
“I will not be silenced,” the congresswoman added.

US Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro also revealed Monday that her office is conducting a separate investigation into Omar’s financial disclosures, which showed her and her husband’s net worth ballooned from between $15,000 and $51,000 in 2023 to between $6 million and $30 million in 2024.
“We’re looking at the facts … we’ll follow them wherever they take us,” Pirro said in an interview with Fox News’ “America Reports.”

articles.headline: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says he won't fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite socialist pressure
keyFacts: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated he has no plans to fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite pressure from democratic socialists.
The pressure followed protests and calls for Tisch's removal after an ICE-involved shooting in the Bronx.
Mamdani defended Tisch by citing her record of lowering crime and reducing corruption within the police department.
body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Tuesday he has "no plans" to fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch, pushing back against calls from his democratic socialist allies to remove the city's top cop following protests over an ICE-involved shooting in the Bronx.
Ahead of a ceremony Tuesday honoring fallen NYPD officers, Mamdani was asked about Tisch's future as head of the department.
"Jessica Tisch is the police commissioner. I have no plans to change that," Mamdani told reporters.

"The reason that I made the decision to have Jessica Tisch as the police commissioner was because of her record of uprooting corruption from the upper echelons of the NYPD while lowering crime across our city," he continued. "And over the last 10 months that we've worked together, we have delivered the lowest recorded number of murders in our city's history, the lowest recorded number of shootings as well as shooting victims."
SOCIALIST SURGE: MAMDANI FLEXES GROWING POLITICAL MUSCLE AS HE TAKES ON DEM ESTABLISHMENT

The mayor's comments came after the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) called for Tisch's removal following last week's ICE shooting and demanded that Mamdani use his authority to drive ICE out of New York City.
The demand followed last week's shooting of Oscar Belgal during a federal immigration operation in the Bronx.

According to the Department of Homeland Security, Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican national, was shot after allegedly refusing to comply with officers' orders during a targeted ICE operation to arrest him.
NYC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE SAYS CRIMINAL RECORD OF MAN SHOT BY ICE 'DOESN'T EVEN MATTER'
Following the incident, a City Hall spokesperson said Mamdani was reviewing the circumstances surrounding the shooting but had no plans to remove Tisch.

Scott Munro, president of the Detectives' Endowment Association — the union representing active and retired NYPD detectives — was also asked by reporters Tuesday about the DSA urging Mamdani to fire Tisch.
Munro said he believes Mamdani supports the police commissioner, noting that crime was down and Tisch was "doing her job."

Mamdani and Tisch appeared together Tuesday at the New York City Police Memorial, where they honored 42 fallen NYPD members, including 41 who died from illnesses related to the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks and their aftermath. The ceremony also honored Detective First Grade Didarul Islam, who was killed in a Midtown Manhattan mass shooting in 2025.
9/11 DEATH TOLL KEEPS GROWING DECADES LATER AS TOXIC EXPOSURE HAUNTS SURVIVORS
The mayor paid tribute to the fallen officers and their families during the ceremony, which Tisch also attended.
"While we cannot feel the silence they left behind, we will refuse to let their memory fade," Mamdani said.
Earlier this week, Mamdani directed the NYPD to conduct a comprehensive review of its use-of-force policies and practices.
He also announced reforms aimed at strengthening accountability when police officers are accused of serious misconduct.

articles.headline: Justice Department says North Koreans have infiltrated dozens of U.S. companies
keyFacts: The U.S. Department of Justice stated that North Korean hackers have infiltrated at least 70 U.S. companies using stolen identities and American facilitators.
Federal prosecutors announced they indicted and arrested at least two people and raided dozens of laptop farms in Texas used for the remote hacking scheme.
The DOJ reported that the scheme generated around $3 million in stolen funds to help fund North Korea's nuclear weapons program.
body: The U.S. Department of Justice is warning that hackers working for the North Korean regime are increasingly relying on Americans to facilitate the hacking of U.S. companies.

In an announcement on Tuesday, prosecutors said they have indicted and arrested at least two people, and conducted searches across dozens of suspected “laptop farms” in Texas. The computers were allegedly used by North Koreans to remotely hack into American companies and steal sensitive data.

According to the DOJ, federal authorities seized over 180 computers that they believe American companies had shipped out to their newly hired employees, not realizing that they were sanctioned North Korean spies who had used stolen identities of U.S. citizens to gain employment. The DOJ said that it raided over 40 laptop farms across Texas, the largest disclosed number of homes and residences used for facilitating North Korean hacks, which were owned by at least two American facilitators.

CrowdStrike, which helped the FBI investigate and disrupt the latest North Korean operations, said that laptop farms are “vital” to North Korea in helping its hackers overcome physical, financial, and legal challenges of not physically being in the United States.

The prosecutors said at least 70 U.S.-based companies had been infiltrated by the hackers, who are believed to have generated around $3 million in stolen funds. The DOJ did not name the affected companies, but described them as healthcare, cyber support, retail, communications, and manufacturing sectors across Ohio and 16 other states, including the District of Columbia.

“Increasingly, North Korean IT workers are turning to recruiting American facilitators to counter improved private sector detections and law enforcement actions. These workers are hiring facilitators to complete a wider variety of tasks, and in some cases subcontracting entire jobs to third-party foreign nationals,” the Justice Department said.
Oftentimes, North Korean hackers use real-looking email addresses, spoofed LinkedIn profiles, and extensive online and social media accounts as cover for their activities.

In a separate public service announcement, the FBI said that there are “thousands” of North Korean-state controlled IT workers working at Western companies, which “pose a significant national security and intellectual property theft insider threat.”

This is the latest wave of arrests, indictments, and enforcement action targeting North Korean activities in the United States in recent years. The breakaway regime has used this “remote IT workers” scheme to allow North Koreans to gain employment with U.S. and European companies, earn a wage, and then steal sensitive information and intellectual property while as employees. The victim companies are then extorted into paying the hackers further.

The remote IT workers’ scheme is one of several strands of illicit revenue that the North Korean regime aims to generate, including hacking crypto exchanges and open-source developer projects, with the aim of funding its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program. The regime is thought to have stolen at least $2 billion in crypto during 2025 alone.
Experts on North Korea have put the number of hacked companies and the amount of stolen crypto as likely much higher than reported.

Earlier this year, CrowdStrike said in a separate report that North Korean hackers were behind around half of all documented “hands-on-keyboard” intrusions over the past year, referring to hacks that are carried out by humans and not automated tools or AI.

articles.headline: Which smart TV brands offer the longest software support?
keyFacts: Smart TV brands offer varying lengths of software support because there is no universal standard across the industry.
Samsung provides seven years of updates for select models, while LG guarantees four years through its webOS Re:New program.
Brands like Sony, TCL, Vizio, and Roku do not guarantee a fixed support period, with updates varying by model.
body: Which smart TV brands offer the longest software support?
Not all smart TVs will receive updates for long, and some don't have any specific policy.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
No matter the price of a TV you buy, you likely consider it as a long-term investment. You thus expect it to receive support from the manufacturer for as long as possible.

In olden times, when you bought a TV, the only worry you had was it eventually breaking. But with smart TVs, there's also software to consider. Most modern TVs come with their own operating systems and apps, and need to be updated semi-regularly for the best performance and to patch security issues.

Unfortunately, there's no universal standard for how long you can expect a TV to get support for. It varies significantly by manufacturer, and the relevant information isn't always easy to find. But you're in luck, as we've done the tedious work of finding out.
Samsung offers long-term software support, but not every brand matches that commitment

If you have a Samsung TV from 2024 or later, Samsung will provide seven years of software updates for its Linux-based Tizen OS. This commitment, made in 2024, also applies to select models from 2023. That means if you have a Samsung TV from 2024, you can expect apps to work smoothly and firmware updates to roll out until at least 2031. Older models won't get major new versions of Tizen. They'll likely receive occasional maintenance or security firmware updates, though.

In early 2024, LG introduced the webOS Re:New program, which guarantees four years of webOS updates for TV models from 2022 onwards. These come with a one-year delay compared to the latest webOS release on the newest TV models. For example, webOS 26 debuted with 2026's TVs, and will come to a 2025 TV one year later.

Sony doesn't offer a fixed period of support for its TVs. Rather, it differs depending on which model you own. For example, for 2025's Sony Bravia K-65XR80M2 OLED, Sony's support page has April 2029 as the end-of-life date. Meanwhile, the Sony Bravia 2 II K-65S25VM2, which was also part of the 2025 lineup, will apparently receive security updates until June 2030.
Unlike LG and Samsung, Sony doesn't have use a proprietary TV operating system. Models released after 2021 use the Google TV platform; prior to that it was Android TV.

Like Sony, TCL doesn't guarantee a fixed period of support. All we really have to go on is the company's Software Security page, where it claims to "typically" provide security updates for at least two years after "the first shipment of a certain device model." This page doesn't explicitly mention TVs, though. Depending on the model, TCL sets primarily run on Google TV (or Android TV for older models) or Roku TV.
Software support also varies by region

In Europe, the majority of Hisense TVs run on the company's proprietary VIDAA OS. Since 2025, it has pledged support for "up to" a whopping eight years on these models. Unfortunately for those in the US, you're less likely to pick up a Hisense TV that uses VIDAA, with many models instead running Android TV, Fire TV, Google TV or Roku TV. Therefore, long-term support is in the hands of the company whose OS your TV ships with.

For a long time, Roku was known for its streaming devices and operating system that it licenses to TV brands like those listed above. But what if you buy one of Roku's own Pro, Plus or Select Series TVs? Roku doesn't specify a fixed period of support for these, and the first came out in 2023, so it's still too early to establish a pattern. But given that software is the company's focus and it frequently pushes out updates, you can reasonably expect a healthy lifespan for its TVs. Roku doesn't publish end-of-life dates for its streaming boxes either, though some people claim to have used one unit for as long as 10 years.

What about the ultra-affordable TV brands like Vizio and Insignia? The former runs its own Vizio OS, which functions in much the same way as its better-known rivals and includes more than 300 apps. Vizio pushes out automatic firmware updates regularly, but doesn't guarantee a fixed period of support for any of its models.

Insignia TVs employ Amazon's Fire OS, so you can assume you'll get software and security updates for as long as Amazon commits to with its own devices. The Amazon Fire TV Software Security Updates page says that commitment is at least four years.
Don't fret once your model is out of support. Buying a streaming box is an inexpensive way to extend your smart TV's life and maintain access to updated versions of your favorite apps.
